newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank raises term rates.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank raises term rates.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Thursday it raised its various reverse repo rates from one month to six months.
Traders said the Central Bank adjusted rates to discourage speculation because the problems of the Thai baht are expected to persist for some months.
"They're pre-empting any speculation by foreign funds," a dealer said.

The one-month reverse repo was raised to 10.625 percent from 10.5 percent; the two months, to 10.75 percent from 10.625 percent; three months, to 10.875 percent from 10.125 percent; and six months, to 11.25 percent from 11.125 percent.
The Central Bank also increased its rate on the three-month special series Treasury-bill to 10.5 percent from 10.2 percent.
Traders said the Central Bank's action signalled that T-bill rates would be higher at next Monday's T-bill auction.
The Central Bank kept its overnight borrowing and lending rates unchanged at 15 percent and 17 percent respectively.
